verses.100:1: A misericórdia e o {judicium} * eu vos cantarei, Senhor:
verses.100:2: Entoarei salmos, e {intellegam} no caminho imaculado, * {quando}
verses.100:2b: Eu andava na inocência do meu coração, * no meio da minha casa.
verses.100:3: Eu não punha diante dos meus olhos coisa injusta: * {odivi} {facientes}.
verses.100:4: Não se apegou a mim coração {pravum}: * {declinantem}
verses.100:5: Quem difamava o seu próximo em segredo, * a {hunc} eu perseguia.
verses.100:6: {oculi}: * quem andava no caminho imaculado, {hic} me servia.
verses.100:7: Não habitará no meio da minha casa quem age com soberba: * quem fala coisas iníquas {direxit} à vista dos meus olhos.
verses.100:8: Pela manhã eu {interficiebam} todos os pecadores da terra: * para exterminar da cidade do Senhor todos os que praticam a iniquidade.

decisions.why: judícium → juízo is settled (D15). Here it stands beside misericórdia as the king's two virtues, and Matos Soares 1932 writes 'justiça'; DRB keeps 'judgment'. 'Justiça' is justítia's word and would merge two Latin nouns; 'juízo' keeps the glossary. Risk: in Brazil 'ter juízo' is good sense — the pairing with misericórdia should steer the ear to judgment.

options.label: juízo
options.note: draft — D15; DRB 'judgment'

options.label: justiça
options.note: MS1932 — explains the sense, but takes justítia's word

options.label: julgamento
options.note: plain, but D15 refused it for the root (rhymes with mandamentos in Ps 118); unambiguous here

decisions.why: intellégere → entender (glossary). 'Entender no caminho' is as unusual in Portuguese as 'intellegere in via' is in Latin (συνήσω ἐν ὁδῷ: to have understanding, to act wisely, in the way). DRB keeps it word for word ('I will understand in the unspotted way'); MS1932 turns it into 'procurarei conhecer o caminho da perfeição', which changes both the verb and the image. The preposition kept: the way is where he understands, not what he understands. Also a Lauds antiphon (Psalmi major, [Day3 Laudes1], i.e. Wednesday: 'Tibi, Dómine, psallam, * et intéllegam in via immaculáta').

options.label: entenderei
options.note: draft — the glossary verb, the Latin's preposition kept; DRB

options.label: terei entendimento
options.note: the root in a noun; smoother with 'no caminho', two syllables longer

options.label: procurarei conhecer (o caminho)
options.note: MS1932's gloss; would also need 'o caminho' for 'no caminho' — refused, another verb and an added effort

decisions.why: Latin 'quando' with a future indicative can be temporal ('when you come to me') or a question ('when will you come to me?'); the Greek πότε ἥξεις and the Hebrew are a question. Portuguese must choose by mood: 'quando vierdes' is only temporal, 'quando vireis?' only a question. The DO Latin ends the verse with a full stop, DRB ('when thou shalt come to me') and MS1932 ('quando vieres a mim') read it as temporal, and the responsory (Epi2-6) sets it as the close of a statement. Ruled temporal; the question kept as an option, since the Greek behind the Latin is interrogative.

options.label: quando vierdes a mim.
options.note: draft — temporal, as DRB, MS1932 and the DO punctuation

options.label: quando vireis a mim?
options.note: the question of the Greek πότε (and of the Hebrew); a Latin reader may hear it too

decisions.why: odívi is read with present sense where its context is present (25:5 'Odeio', 118:104 'odeio' — the review's ruling). Here it stands inside a narrative of imperfects (proponébam, cognoscébam, persequébar, edébam), so the perfect's past is the natural reading: DRB 'I hated', the Greek aorist ἐμίσησα. MS1932 has the imperfect 'aborrecia'. Ruled 'odiei', the perfect for the perfect; the verb first (natural order), the object after it.

options.label: odiei
options.note: draft — perfect, DRB 'I hated', ἐμίσησα

options.label: odiava
options.note: in step with the surrounding imperfects; MS1932 'aborrecia' — but the Latin changes tense here

options.label: odeio
options.note: the present sense ruled in 25:5 and 118:104; jars inside a past narrative

decisions.why: prævaricatiónes → 'transgressões', the noun of 118:119/158 'transgressores' (the cognate 'prevaricação' is administrative law in Brazil). fácere with it: 'fazer transgressões' is the calque; 'cometer' is the verb Portuguese uses with the noun — a collocation, not a new sense (D2: the plainer of two faithful words). The participle put in the past, in step with the verse's narrative (MS1932 'os que cometiam').

options.label: os que cometiam transgressões
options.note: draft — MS1932's verb; the glossary's noun

options.label: os que faziam transgressões
options.note: fácere → fazer, as the row fácere iniquitátem (36:1); stiffer

options.label: os que cometem transgressões
options.note: the participle timeless, as in the formula 'os que praticam a iniquidade' (100:8)

decisions.why: pravus is 'crooked', then 'perverse'; the Greek here is σκαμβή, 'crooked, bent'. Ps 77 has both uses: 77:8 generátio prava → 'geração perversa', 77:57 arcum pravum → 'um arco torto'. For a heart the moral sense is the one the Latin reader hears; 'perverso' matches 77:8. 'torto' keeps the image of the bent thing and is kept as the option. No article, as the Latin, and as MS1932 ('Não se unia a mim coração depravado'): 'any perverse heart'.

options.label: perverso
options.note: draft — as 77:8

options.label: torto
options.note: the image of σκαμβή and of 77:57; odd for a heart in Portuguese

options.label: depravado
options.note: MS1932; the cognate, heard today as sexual vice

decisions.latin: declinántem a me malígnum non cognoscébam
decisions.why: The participle goes with malígnum: 'the malign man who turned aside from me I did not know' (DRB). malígnus → 'malvado' (D24), declináre a → 'apartar-se de' (glossary). The Latin puts the object first; unlike 100:5 and 5b it has no resumptive pronoun. Natural Portuguese order puts the verb first, and 'eu' must be named because 'conhecia' is also third person (the ear could make 'coração perverso' its subject). MS1932 splits it into two clauses ('o mau afastava-se de mim, e eu não o conhecia'), which makes the turning away a fact rather than a description — refused.

options.label: eu não conhecia o malvado que se apartava de mim.

forms.declinantem: eu não conhecia o malvado que se apartava de mim.

options.note: draft — natural order; the verse's two colons both open with 'não'-clauses

options.label: o malvado que se apartava de mim, eu não o conhecia.

forms.declinantem: o malvado que se apartava de mim, eu não o conhecia.

options.note: the Latin's order, with a resumptive pronoun Portuguese needs; matches 100:5, 5b, 6b

forms.declinantem: o malvado afastava-se de mim, e eu não o conhecia.

decisions.why: Two ablatives of quality describing the person whom 'cum hoc' then resumes; the Latin names no noun and no verb. Portuguese needs one of the two: a verb ('quem tinha', built like 100:5 'Quem difamava … a esse') or a noun (MS1932 'Com homem de olhos soberbos'). The verb keeps the two verses parallel as the Latin's are (participle / ablatives, then hunc / hoc). 'ter o coração X' is the build of 4:3 ('tereis o coração pesado'). Singular 'olho', as the Latin (glossary: óculus singular where the Latin is).

options.label: Quem tinha o olho soberbo e o coração insaciável

decisions.latin: hunc persequébar · cum hoc non edébam · hic mihi ministrábat
decisions.why: Three resumptive demonstratives take up the person just described; the Latin repeats hic, so the Portuguese repeats one word. The glossary's 'hic est → este é' (D43) is for a pointing 'this'; for a pronoun that takes up what was just said Brazilian usage is 'esse', as MS1932 has twice ('com esse não comia', 'esse me servia').

options.label: esse
options.note: draft — MS1932 in 5b and 6

options.label: este
options.note: hic → este, as D43; heard as more pointed

decisions.latin: Óculi mei ad fidéles terræ ut sédeant mecum
decisions.why: The first clause has no verb; Portuguese needs one (a copula, D2). Its tense is open in the Latin: 'sédeant' is present, 'ministrábat' in the second colon past. DRB ('My eyes were upon') and MS1932 ('buscavam') put it in the past with the narrative of 100:2b–6; ruled so. 'para se sentarem' (DRB 'to sit with me') leaves the tense of the purpose unmarked and is two syllables shorter than 'para que se sentassem'. 'estavam nos fiéis' for 'ad': eyes resting on someone; 'voltados para' (9:30a's formula for 'in … respíciunt') is closer to 'ad' but longer. MS1932's 'buscavam' supplies a verb of meaning — refused.

options.label: Os meus olhos estavam nos fiéis da terra, para se sentarem comigo

decisions.latin: non diréxit in conspéctu oculórum meórum
decisions.why: dirígere without an object (κατεύθυνεν): 'went straight', and so 'held his course, prospered'. The same Latin build in 58:5 ('sine iniquitáte cucúrri, et diréxi') is 'segui reto', and the same words keep the same Portuguese. DRB 'did not prosper' interprets toward success; MS1932 'não pôde tornar-se agradável aos meus olhos' paraphrases. 'não seguiu reto' keeps the Latin's image and its double sense (did not go straight / did not get on). in conspéctu oculórum → 'à vista dos meus olhos', as 17:25.

options.label: não seguiu reto
options.note: draft — = 58:5 'segui reto'

options.label: não prosperou
options.note: DRB 'did not prosper'; one sense of two

options.label: não se manteve de pé
options.note: 'was not established'; interprets

decisions.why: The glossary row interfícere / occídere → assassinar / matar (open) was made for 93:6, where the two verbs stand side by side and must differ. Alone, interfícere is 'matar' in 9:29 ('para matar o inocente'). Here the king puts evildoers to death at the morning court; 'assassinar' is 'murder', a judgment the Latin does not make. DRB 'I put to death'; MS1932 'exterminava' spends dispérdere's word, which follows in the same verse.

options.label: matava
options.note: draft — as 9:29

options.label: fazia morrer
options.note: DRB 'put to death'; softer, longer

options.label: assassinava
options.note: the row's word from 93:6; 'murder'

choices.100:1: The article supplied before both nouns (the object fronted, as in the Latin). 'eu vos cantarei': the subject named so the colon does not open on a clitic. cantáre → cantar here, psállere → 'entoar salmos' in the next verse (D25) — the two verbs kept apart as the Latin keeps them. Responsory R. of Epi2-6 opens with this verse.
choices.100:2: psállere → 'Entoarei salmos' (D25). immaculátus → 'imaculado' (glossary; 17:33, 118:1); 'no caminho imaculado' is repeated identically at 100:6, as the Latin repeats 'in via immaculáta'. The Lauds antiphon (Psalmi major, Day3 Laudes1) 'Tibi, Dómine, psallam, * et intéllegam in via immaculáta' would read 'A vós, Senhor, entoarei salmos, * e entenderei no caminho imaculado'.
choices.100:2b: perambuláre → 'andar' (the row names 100:2 for L&S's Church sense, 'walk, conduct oneself'). The versicle of Epi2-6 reads it alone; it stands alone.
choices.100:3: 'Eu' named: 'punha' is also third person. rem injústam → 'coisa injusta', no article (MS1932's wording). prævaricatiónes → 'transgressões', the noun of 118:119 'transgressores'.
choices.100:4: adhærére → 'apegar-se a' (24:21, 62:9, 72:28, 93:20). The two colons open 'Não … / eu não …', the Latin's two negatives.
choices.100:5: detráhere + dative → 'difamar' (settled, D39; the row names 100:5). 'o seu próximo' moved off the mediant (a proparoxytone at a cadence — glossary row próximus), and 'em segredo' (secréto) takes the cadence. The preposed 'a esse' is the Latin's fronted 'hunc'.
choices.100:5b: édere → 'comer' (glossary). The -ia imperfects at the finals of 100:5, 5b, 6 (perseguia, comia, servia) echo as the Latin's -bar / -bam / -bat do: accepted as the Latin's own echo.
choices.100:6: 'os fiéis da terra' as 118:119 'os pecadores da terra', and 100:8 below. ministráre → 'servir' (DRB, MS1932 'esse me servia'); servíre's imperative is 'Sede servos' (D18), and the two Latin verbs never meet in a verse. 'quem andava' for the participle 'ámbulans', in step with 'ministrábat'.
choices.100:7: fácere supérbiam → 'agir com soberba' (row, 30:24). loqui iníqua → 'falar coisas iníquas' (the neuter plural as 25:4 'coisas iníquas'). The future 'Não habitará' kept: the Latin moves from past to future here.
choices.100:8: in matutíno → 'Pela manhã', as 48:15b (in matutíno), kept apart from mane → 'de manhã'. dispérdere → 'exterminar' (glossary). operántes iniquitátem → 'os que praticam a iniquidade' (formula, 5:7a, 93:16). 'omnes peccatóres terræ' = 118:119 'todos os pecadores da terra'. 'para exterminar' for ut + subjunctive with the same subject (grammar).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps100.md (no Diurnal section for this psalm). Glossary rows read for every controlled word (ps100/gloss_grep.py); finished psalms consulted for adhærére, pravus, dirígere absolute (58:5), in matutíno (48:15b), interfícere (9:29), in conspéctu oculórum (17:25), prævaricántes (118:119). Liturgical uses found by grep: responsory and versicle in Tempora/Epi2-6 (100:1–2b), antiphon 'Tibi, Dómine, psallam' in Psalmi major. Hard readings: 100:2 'quando vénies' (temporal or question), 100:3 odívi in a past narrative, 100:6 the verbless first clause, 100:7 'non diréxit' absolute.

Hard checks pass. Soft: length +5 at 100:2a (psállere → 'entoar salmos' is two words for one, D25, and 'imaculado' is long) and 100:6a (a copula supplied for the verbless clause); +4 at 100:4a/b (the reflexive 'se apegou a mim'; 'eu' named against a third-person hearing) and 100:5b (a verb supplied for the ablatives of quality); +3 at 100:5b ('a esse eu' for 'hunc'). Each is one breath; accepted. Rhyme flag -ia at the finals of 100:5, 5b, 6 (perseguia / comia / servia): the Latin's own echo (persequébar / edébam / ministrábat), accepted.
